title: Corporate Balance Due Date Calculator | Two or Three Months
content:
Date Tool

Corporate Balance Due Date Calculator

Paying a balance of tax is due before the return is. Enter the fiscal year-end for both dates, on the same holiday calendar.

Two months, or three for a CCPCFiling stays at six monthsMoved off weekends and holidaysNothing to pay on a nil year

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

Your fiscal year-end

Enter the year-end and answer the question for both dates.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Filing and Paying Are Two Different Deadlines

Almost everything written about the T2 gives one date: six months after the fiscal year-end. That is the date the return is due. It is not the date a balance of tax is due, and the balance date comes first.

A balance is due two months after the year-end, or three months for a Canadian-controlled private corporation that meets the conditions. A corporation that files on the six-month date and pays at the same time has filed on time and paid late.

On a Nil Year Only One of Them Applies

A corporation with no activity has no balance to pay, so the earlier date passes with nothing owed on it. It also has no instalment obligation, because that arises from the previous year’s tax and a nil year sets that at $0.00.

That leaves the filing deadline as the only date a dormant corporation has to meet, which is the whole of its tax calendar. The nil T2 deadline calculator gives that date on its own.

A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

Where the Three-Month Period Comes From

The longer period is not available to every small corporation. It turns on the corporation being a Canadian-controlled private corporation and on conditions about its income and its taxable capital being met, in the year and in the one before it.

This calculator takes the answer as given rather than deciding it, because the conditions rest on figures a dormant corporation does not have and a trading one should not read off a web page. Where the answer is not certain, the two-month date is the safe one to work to.

Both Dates Move Off a Weekend or a Holiday

Where either calculated date falls on a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday, it moves to the next business day. The calculation here runs on the same holiday calendar as the deadline pages, so the two never disagree.

The shift can be more than one day. A date landing on a Sunday followed by a Monday holiday moves to the Tuesday, which the due date weekend and holiday shift calculator shows on its own.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is a corporate balance of tax due?

Two months after the fiscal year-end, or three months for a Canadian-controlled private corporation that meets the conditions. Filing the return is separately due six months after the year-end.

Does a nil year have a balance due date?

The date exists but nothing is owed on it. A corporation with no activity has no balance of tax and no instalment obligation, which leaves the six-month filing deadline as the only date it has to meet.

Can I pay when I file?

Only where the two dates coincide, which they do not. A corporation that pays a balance on the six-month filing date has paid four months late, or three.

Which period applies to my corporation?

The three-month period turns on Canadian-controlled private corporation status and on conditions about income and taxable capital in this year and the one before. Where that is not certain, work to the two-month date.

What if the date falls on a holiday?

It moves to the next business day, on the same holiday calendar the filing deadline uses. The shift can be more than one day where a holiday sits next to a weekend.

title: Fiscal Period Length Calculator | Days, Weeks and the 53-Week Limit
content:
Date Tool

Fiscal Period Length Calculator

Enter the first and last day of a fiscal period for its length in days and weeks, whether it clears the 53-week limit, and its T2 date.

Counts both endsTests the 371-day limitShort years get the same six monthsGives the filing date

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

The fiscal period

Enter both days and the length appears here.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Why the Length of a Period Is Worth Measuring

Three rules turn on how long a fiscal period is, and all three are easy to get wrong by a few days. A first tax year may not exceed 53 weeks. A period shorter than twelve months is a short tax year. A period longer than twelve months is not a tax year at all.

Counting it by eye from two dates in different years is where the mistakes come from. This counts the days, including both the first and the last, and converts them to weeks.

The 53-Week Limit Is 371 Days

A first tax year runs from the date of incorporation to the chosen year-end and may not exceed 53 weeks, which is 371 days counting the day of incorporation. A year-end chosen beyond that is not available.

Where a period here comes out longer, and it is a first year, the year-end has to fall earlier. That produces a short first year followed by a full one, and two returns due within a few months of each other. The 53-week first tax year checker tests that question on its own.

A Short Period Still Gets the Full Six Months

The six-month rule is measured from the day the period ends, whatever its length. A three-month stub period still has six months after it to file, which is longer than the period itself.

Short periods arise on a first year, on an approved change of year-end, on an amalgamation and on a final year ending at dissolution. Each is a separate return at $300.00 plus HST per tax year. The short tax year deadline calculator goes further into the filing date.

Changing a Year-End Needs Written Approval

A fiscal year-end is fixed by the first return filed, and changing it needs the written approval of the Canada Revenue Agency. A return filed with a different date on it does not change the year-end on record, it is rejected against it.

An approved change produces a short period, and this calculator will measure it. What it cannot do is tell you the change was approved.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long can a first tax year be?

Up to 53 weeks, which is 371 days counting the day of incorporation. A year-end chosen beyond that is not available, so the first year has to end earlier.

Does a short tax year have an earlier deadline?

No. The six-month rule is measured from the day the short period ends, so a three-month period still has six months after it to file.

Is a period longer than twelve months a tax year?

No. A tax year cannot exceed 53 weeks, so a longer period means the year-end being used is not the one on record, or the dates are wrong.

Does this count the first and last day?

Yes, both. A period from January 1 to December 31 counts as 365 days in an ordinary year, not 364.

How do I change my fiscal year-end?

With the written approval of the Canada Revenue Agency. Filing a return carrying a different date does not change the year-end on record.

title: CRA Demand to File Deadline Calculator | Days Left to Respond
content:
Demand to File

CRA Demand to File Deadline Calculator

A demand to file names a date. Enter the letter date and the days it allows for the deadline, the days left and the business days left.

Counts calendar and business daysMoves off weekends and holidaysSays when the date has passedFiling is what answers a demand

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

The letter

Enter the letter date and the days it allows.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

What a Demand to File Changes

A demand to file is a formal written requirement to file a named return by a named date. It converts an overdue return into a legal obligation with its own deadline, and that date is the one this calculator works to.

The number of days a demand allows is stated on the letter rather than fixed in advance, which is why it is typed in here rather than assumed. Reading it off the letter is the one step that cannot be skipped.

What Happens If the Date Passes

Where a demand goes unanswered the Canada Revenue Agency may assess the corporation on its own estimate of income. That assessment creates a real balance, interest runs on it, and it stands until a filed return displaces it.

This is how a dormant corporation that genuinely owed nothing ends up with a collectible debt. The balance was not produced by activity. It was produced by the missing return, which is also what removes it.

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

Filing Is What Answers a Demand

Nothing else closes it. A demand names a return, and the return being filed is the response. Where several years are outstanding they are prepared oldest first, so the closing balances of one open the next, and they can be transmitted together.

Each year is its own return at $300.00 plus HST per tax year. The unfiled years checker lists which years are outstanding, and the unfiled years cost calculator totals them.

Why Business Days Are Counted Separately

The calendar count is what the letter runs on. The business-day count is what the work runs on, and on a short deadline the two differ enough to matter: ten calendar days over a long weekend is six business days.

Where the named date itself falls on a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday, it moves to the next business day, on the same holiday calendar the filing deadlines use.

Frequently Asked Questions

How long does a demand to file give me?

The letter states the date or the number of days. It is not a fixed period, which is why it has to be read off the letter rather than assumed.

What happens if I ignore a demand to file?

The Canada Revenue Agency may assess the corporation on its own estimate of income. That arbitrary assessment is collectible and stands until the actual return displaces it.

Does a nil return answer a demand?

Yes. The demand names a return, and filing that return answers it. A year with no activity is filed showing $0.00 and the demand is closed.

Can I ask for more time?

That is a matter for the Agency and the particular letter. What does not help is letting the date pass without filing, because that is what an arbitrary assessment follows from.

What if the named date is a weekend?

It moves to the next business day, on the same holiday calendar the T2 filing deadline uses.

title: T4 Nil Filing Requirement Checker | Open Payroll Account
content:
Payroll

T4 Nil Filing Requirement Checker

An open payroll account expects a T4 information return even where nobody was paid. Three answers give the date and what is owed.

Due the end of FebruaryExpected while the account is openForm RC145 closes itNot covered by the nil T2 fee

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

The payroll account

Enter the year and answer both questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The T4 Runs on the Calendar Year, Not Your Year-End

Almost every other date on this site is measured from the fiscal year-end. The T4 information return is not. It reports a calendar year and is due at the end of the following February, whatever year-end the corporation uses.

A corporation with a June 30 year-end therefore has a T2 date in December and a T4 date at the end of February, four months apart and neither derived from the other.

An Open Account Expects a Return Either Way

The obligation follows the account, not the activity. While a payroll account is open, the Agency expects the annual information return and expects the remittances through the year, including nil ones.

That is the trap for a dormant corporation: it stopped paying anyone years ago, and the account is still open and still generating dates. The payroll nil remittance checker covers the remittances; this page covers the annual return.

Form RC145 Is What Stops It

Closing the payroll account with Form RC145 is the only thing that ends the obligation. Until it is closed the dates recur every year, and nothing about the corporation being dormant pauses them.

Closing the account is not covered by the nil T2 fee, and neither is the T4 return itself. The fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year covers one nil T2 return for one corporation for one tax year, and the nil T2 filing cost page sets out what sits outside it.

Why This One Reaches the Directors

Payroll source deductions are money withheld from someone’s pay and owed to the Agency. Amounts of that kind can be assessed against directors personally, which corporate income tax on its own cannot.

That is the practical reason an unused payroll account is worth closing rather than ignoring. The director liability exposure checker sets out which amounts reach a director and which do not.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the T4 information return due?

The end of February following the calendar year it reports. It is measured from the calendar year, not from the corporation’s fiscal year-end.

Do I file a T4 return if nobody was paid?

While the payroll account is open the return is expected, and so are the nil remittances through the year. Closing the account with Form RC145 is what ends both.

Is the T4 return covered by the nil T2 fee?

No. The fee covers one nil T2 return for one corporation for one tax year. The T4 return, the nil remittances and the account closure all sit outside it.

How do I close a payroll account?

With Form RC145. Until it is closed the account keeps generating obligations whether or not the corporation is doing anything.

Does an open payroll account affect my nil T2?

Not the T2 itself, which is still nil where there was no activity. What it affects is everything alongside the T2, and the directors’ personal exposure to unremitted amounts.

title: Retained Earnings Rollforward Calculator | Opening to Closing
content:
Schedule 100

Retained Earnings Rollforward Calculator

Opening, plus net income, less dividends, gives closing. The figure the next return has to open from, and what it says about nil status.

Three figures in, one outThe next year opens from itHandles a deficitShows what ends a nil year

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

The three figures

Enter all three figures. Use 0 where there was nothing.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Whole Calculation Is One Line

Opening retained earnings, plus net income for the year, less dividends declared, gives closing retained earnings. There is nothing else in it, and the arithmetic can be checked by hand in a second.

What makes it worth a page is not the arithmetic. It is that the closing figure is the number the next return has to open from, and a return that does not carry it forward is rejected rather than filed.

On a Quiet Year the Figure Does Not Move

A year with no net income and no dividends closes exactly where it opened. That is the ordinary shape of a nil year: the income statement reports zeroes while the balance sheet still carries real numbers.

Retained earnings brought forward are one of three balances that commonly sit on a nil return’s balance sheet, alongside share capital issued on incorporation and a shareholder loan. The nil GIFI balance sheet checker tests which of them apply.

Net Income or a Dividend Ends the Nil Year

Either figure being something other than zero means the year was not nil. A dividend declared is activity whether or not it was paid in cash, and net income is activity by definition.

A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

The nil return versus full return checker works through the whole test rather than these two lines.

A Deficit Is the Same Calculation

Where the closing figure is negative the corporation has a deficit rather than retained earnings. It sits in the same place on Schedule 100 and carries forward the same way.

A corporation that spent money before it earned any, which is most corporations in their first year or two, will show a deficit. It is unremarkable and it does not change what is filed.

Frequently Asked Questions

How is closing retained earnings calculated?

Opening retained earnings, plus net income for the year, less dividends declared. The closing figure is what the next return opens from.

Does retained earnings change on a nil year?

No. With no net income and no dividends the closing figure equals the opening one, and the balance simply carries forward.

Where does this figure go on the return?

On Schedule 100, the balance sheet, reported through the coded GIFI format. A nil year files it carrying the balances it holds.

What if the figure is negative?

That is a deficit rather than retained earnings. It sits in the same place and carries forward the same way, and it is common in a corporation’s first years.

Does a dividend end a nil year even if unpaid?

A dividend declared is activity, so that year is not a nil year. Those returns are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

title: Balance Sheet Balancing Checker | Schedule 100 Validation
content:
Schedule 100

Balance Sheet Balancing Checker

Assets must equal liabilities plus equity or Schedule 100 will not validate. Enter the three totals to see the difference.

Three totals inNames the differenceLists the usual causesA rejection, not a late filing

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

The three totals

Enter all three totals. Use 0 where there is nothing.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

An Unbalanced Sheet Is a Rejection, Not a Late Filing

Schedule 100 will not validate where assets do not equal liabilities plus equity. The consequence is not a late return, it is a transmission the Agency refuses, and a refused transmission is not a filed return.

That distinction matters on a catch-up, where several years are being sent in one sitting. One year that will not balance stops the sequence, because the next year opens from its closing figures.

The Three Causes Worth Checking First

Share capital left off the equity side is the commonest. A corporation that issued shares on incorporation has share capital whether or not anyone thinks of it as money, and a balance sheet filed as all zeroes omits it.

A shareholder loan on the wrong side is the second. A balance owed to a shareholder is a liability; a balance owed by one is an asset, and they are not interchangeable.

Retained earnings not carried forward is the third. The retained earnings rollforward calculator gives the figure the current year has to open from.

A Nil Year Still Has to Balance

The income statement reporting zeroes does not make the balance sheet optional. Schedule 100 is filed on a nil year carrying whatever the corporation holds, and it has to balance like any other.

A genuinely empty corporation, holding nothing and owing nothing, balances trivially at zero on all three lines. Most dormant corporations are not quite that empty.

What This Checker Does Not Do

It compares three totals you supply. It cannot tell you whether the totals are right, whether an item sits in the correct category, or whether a balance belongs on the return at all.

A sheet that balances can still be wrong, and a sheet that balances at the wrong figures will transmit cleanly. This finds one specific defect, which is the one that stops a transmission.

Frequently Asked Questions

What happens if my balance sheet does not balance?

Schedule 100 will not validate and the transmission is refused. A refused transmission is not a filed return, so the year stays outstanding.

Does a nil return still file a balance sheet?

Yes. Schedule 100 is filed carrying whatever the corporation holds, even where the income statement reports nothing but zeroes.

What usually causes the difference?

Share capital left off the equity side, a shareholder loan on the wrong side, or retained earnings not carried forward from the previous year’s closing figure.

Which side does a shareholder loan go on?

A balance owed to a shareholder is a liability. A balance owed by a shareholder to the corporation is an asset. They are not interchangeable.

Can a balance sheet balance and still be wrong?

Yes. This checks one specific defect, the one that stops a transmission. It cannot tell you whether the totals themselves are right.

title: Nil GIFI Balance Sheet Checker | What Schedule 100 Must Carry
content:
Schedule 100

Nil GIFI Balance Sheet Checker

A nil return is not an empty return. Four answers show which balances Schedule 100 has to carry, and which end the nil year.

Four questionsNames each balance and its placeCatches the all-zero mistakeFlags the bank interest trap

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

What the corporation holds

Answer all four questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

A Nil Return Is Not an Empty Return

This is the single most common misunderstanding about nil filing. The income statement reports zeroes, because nothing happened. The balance sheet reports what the corporation holds, because it holds it whether or not anything happened.

Share capital issued on incorporation, a shareholder loan and retained earnings brought forward all sit on Schedule 100 on a year where the corporation did nothing at all.

Filing It as All Zeroes Is Wrong in a Way That Persists

A balance sheet filed as entirely zero when share capital was issued is wrong, and the error does not stay in one year. The next return opens from the closing balances this one reports, so a wrong closing figure is a wrong opening figure next time.

On a catch-up this compounds. Six years filed from a zeroed balance sheet are six years that will not reconcile against the corporate record, and the reconciliation is what a clearance request eventually rests on.

The Bank Balance Is Also the Nil-Status Trap

A bank balance belongs on the asset side, which is this page’s subject. It is also the commonest way a quiet year stops being nil, because interest credited to a corporate account is investment income whatever the amount.

Four dollars of interest answers that question the same way four thousand would. A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

The Other Schedules a Nil Year Carries

Schedule 100 is the balance sheet, Schedule 125 the income statement and Schedule 141 the notes checklist. Schedule 24 appears on a first return only, and Schedule 50 reports every shareholder at 10% or more.

The GIFI schedule requirement checker works out which are required, and the balance sheet balancing checker tests whether the one here will validate.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is a nil return’s balance sheet all zeroes?

Rarely. Share capital issued on incorporation, a shareholder loan and retained earnings brought forward all sit on Schedule 100 whether or not anything happened during the year.

What if I filed it as all zeroes?

The closing figures are wrong, and the next return opens from them, so the error carries forward rather than staying in one year.

Does a bank balance end a nil year?

The balance itself does not. Interest credited on it is investment income whatever the amount, and that does.

Where does share capital go?

On the equity side of Schedule 100. A corporation that issued shares on incorporation has share capital even where no money changed hands in the year.

Which schedules does a nil year file?

Schedules 100, 125 and 141 where required, Schedule 24 on a first return only, Schedule 50 for every shareholder at 10% or more, and Schedule 8 where depreciable property is held.

title: Schedule 8 CCA Requirement Checker | Depreciable Property
content:
Schedule 8

Schedule 8 CCA Requirement Checker

Three answers on whether Schedule 8 belongs on the return, why a carried balance is enough on its own, and what a disposal changes.

Three questionsA carried balance is enoughClaiming nothing is a choiceA disposal ends the nil year

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

Depreciable property

Answer all three questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

What Schedule 8 Reports

Schedule 8 records capital cost allowance and the undepreciated balance carried forward. It is the schedule that tracks what the corporation owns in the way of equipment, vehicles and similar property, and how much of their cost is still to be claimed.

It is filed with the T2 where the corporation holds depreciable property, and a nil year files it like any other year.

A Carried Balance Is Enough on Its Own

The schedule is not required only where something was bought or claimed. An undepreciated balance brought forward from an earlier year is enough: the balance has to be carried, and Schedule 8 is where it is carried.

That is why a dormant corporation that bought a van four years ago and has done nothing since still files Schedule 8. The van did not stop existing because the corporation stopped trading.

Claiming Nothing in a Quiet Year Is a Choice

Capital cost allowance is a claim, not an obligation. A corporation with no income has nothing to reduce, so claiming allowance in a nil year generally achieves nothing and simply shrinks the balance available later.

The balance carries forward either way, which is the point of the schedule. The guide to Schedule 8 and loss continuity goes further into the interaction with losses.

A Disposal Ends the Nil Year

Selling or transferring depreciable property is a disposition, and a disposition is activity. The year it happened in is not a nil year, whatever else the corporation did or did not do.

A holding corporation with investment income, a rental corporation and a corporation that paid or received a dividend are not nil. Those are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

This matters most at a wind-up, because a corporation cannot be dissolved holding property. The dissolution readiness checker covers that sequence.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is Schedule 8 required?

Where the corporation holds depreciable property, or carries an undepreciated balance from an earlier year. Either one on its own is enough.

Does a nil year file Schedule 8?

Yes, where depreciable property is held or a balance is carried forward. The property does not stop existing because the corporation stopped trading.

Do I have to claim capital cost allowance?

No. It is a claim rather than an obligation, and a corporation with no income has nothing to reduce. The balance carries forward either way.

What if I sold the property during the year?

A disposition is activity, so that year is not a nil year. Those returns are handled by Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca at $350.00 plus HST per year.

Is Schedule 8 covered by the fee?

Yes. Where the year is nil, Schedule 8 and the loss continuity are recorded within the fee of $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

title: Involuntary Dissolution Risk Checker | Struck by the Registry
content:
Registry

Involuntary Dissolution Risk Checker

A missed annual return gets a corporation struck, not charged. Three answers on the exposure and why the tax years survive it.

Three registry questionsStriking, not a chargeThe tax years survive itRevival is the way back

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

The registry record

Answer all three questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

A Missed Annual Return Produces a Striking

The annual return is a registry filing, not a tax return. It confirms the directors, the registered office and that the corporation still exists, and it reports no income.

Missing it does not produce a charge. It produces a striking: the registry dissolves the corporation involuntarily. A corporation can be perfectly current on tax and still be dissolved this way, which is the part that surprises people.

A Stale Address Is What Makes It Happen Quietly

The registry sends its warning to the registered office. Where that address is a former accountant’s office or a home the shareholder moved out of, the warning arrives nowhere and the striking happens without anyone noticing.

A dormant corporation is the most likely to be in exactly this position, because nobody is checking the post at an office nobody uses. Keeping the address current is the least demanding piece of maintenance there is, and the one most often left.

The Tax Years Survive the Striking

Being struck settles nothing with the Canada Revenue Agency. The corporation’s tax years stay open and unfiled, and an unfiled year does not expire. A corporation struck in 2021 still owes every return it owed in 2021.

That is why a striking is not a way of closing a corporation. It ends the legal existence and leaves the tax side exactly as it was, which is the opposite of a clean wind-up.

Revival Is the Way Back

Registries provide for revival, which restores the corporation so the outstanding filings can be made and a proper wind-up completed. The open tax years are waiting, and they are filed oldest first.

Each year is its own return at $300.00 plus HST per tax year. The guide to winding up an inactive corporation sets out the order the steps have to happen in.

Frequently Asked Questions

What happens if I miss the annual return?

The registry can dissolve the corporation involuntarily. That is a striking rather than a charge, and it can happen while the corporation is fully current on tax.

Does being struck close my tax account?

No. The tax years stay open and unfiled, and an unfiled year does not expire. A striking ends the legal existence and settles nothing on the tax side.

Why did I not get a warning?

The registry writes to the registered office. Where that address is out of date the warning arrives nowhere, which is how most strikings happen unnoticed.

Can a struck corporation be restored?

Registries provide for revival, which restores it so the outstanding filings can be made and a proper wind-up completed.

Is the annual return covered by the nil T2 fee?

No. It is a registry filing and sits outside the fee, which covers one nil T2 return for one corporation for one tax year.

title: Director Liability Exposure Checker | Which Amounts Reach You
content:
Directors

Director Liability Exposure Checker

Payroll source deductions and net GST/HST can be assessed against directors personally. Corporate income tax on its own cannot.

Three questionsWithheld money reaches youCorporate tax on its own does notClosing accounts ends it

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: October 29, 2026

What the corporation owes

Answer all three questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Pattern Is Money That Was Never the Corporation’s

Certain amounts a corporation was required to withhold or collect and remit can be assessed against its directors personally. Payroll source deductions and net GST/HST are the two that matter here.

The reason is that the money was never the corporation’s to keep. Source deductions were withheld from someone’s pay and GST/HST was collected from customers, both on the Agency’s behalf. Corporate income tax is different: it is the corporation’s own liability, and on its own it does not reach a director.

Why This Reaches Dormant Corporations

A dormant corporation rarely owes corporate income tax, because a nil year assesses at $0.00. What it often has is an account nobody closed: a payroll account from when it had staff, or a GST/HST account from when it was registered.

While those accounts are open they keep generating obligations, and the amounts they generate are exactly the ones that reach directors. That is the practical case for closing them rather than ignoring them.

A true nil return carries no percentage late-filing penalty, because that penalty is a percentage of tax owing and the corporation owes $0.00. The unfiled year still stays open forever, invites a demand to file and an arbitrary assessment, blocks a clearance certificate and dissolution, and costs a non-resident-owned corporation $25.00 per day up to $2,500.00.

Closing the Accounts Is What Ends It

Form RC145 closes a GST/HST account and a payroll account. Until an account is closed, nil returns and nil remittances remain due on it, separately from the T2.

Neither closure is covered by the nil T2 fee. The GST/HST account closure checker and the payroll nil remittance checker each cover one of them.

What This Checker Is Not

It sorts three kinds of amount into the ones that can reach a director and the one that does not. It does not assess whether a particular director is liable, which turns on facts about the director and the period that no web page can take in.

Where an assessment has been raised or threatened against a director personally, that is a matter for Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca rather than a form on this site.

Frequently Asked Questions

Which corporate amounts can reach a director personally?

Amounts the corporation was required to withhold or collect and remit, including payroll source deductions and net GST/HST.

Does corporate income tax reach directors?

Not on its own. It is the corporation’s own liability, collectible from the corporation, and the Agency has statutory collection powers it can use without going to court.

Why does this matter to a dormant corporation?

Because a nil year owes no corporate income tax but an unclosed payroll or GST/HST account keeps generating exactly the amounts that do reach directors.

How do I end the exposure?

Close the accounts. Form RC145 closes a GST/HST account and a payroll account, and until then nil returns and nil remittances remain due on them.

Is an assessment against me personally covered here?

No. That turns on facts about the director and the period, and it is a matter for Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation at gondaliyacpa.ca.
